newsitem.title: ESTONIA: NRG signs joint venture power deal with Estonia.
newsitem.headline: NRG signs joint venture power deal with Estonia.

text.p: NRG Energy, part of Northern States Power, Friday signed a deal with the Estonian goverment and power producer Estonian Energy and to create a joint venture to operate Estonia's two biggest power plants.
NRG Energy intends to invest about $250 million in the venture, the biggest foreign investment so far in the former Soviet state.
The project consists of a business plan and a techical and economic analysis of the two plants, both of which use oil shale and produce some 96 percent of Estonian electricity.

"Our goal is to create a strong power company in cooperation with Estonian Energy effectively to produce electricity for the Estonian people as well as industry," David Peterson, NRG Energy chief, told a news conference.
He said the power may also be exported, and that the deal would solve potential environmental, social and economic problems.
Arvi Hamburg, economy minister deputy chancellor, said other potential investors still have the chance to take part in the privatisation of the transmission and distribution network.
NRG's stock closed Thursday at $46 on the New York Stock Exchange.
